title: What customers actually saw
lede: Screenshots of pages saved by the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine, stored as images. Click one to open the original capture.[^38]

snips.text: “Make your next VCR a TiVo!” **$99.99** after rebates: $299.99, less a $100 Circuit City mail-in rebate and a $100 manufacturer rebate with service activation.
“Free shipping on orders $24 & up or choose 24-minute in-store pickup”

note: Captures from 1997 to 1999 exist but most of their images were never archived, and the 2004 captures redirect to an error, so they are not shown.

captures.label: The 2000 store
captures.title: Price, selection, service
captures.text: The web store a year after launch. The menu still lists appliances three weeks after the company said it would stop selling them.[^5] Cropped to the page content.

captures.label: Ten days before
captures.title: Two days before the store-closing announcement
captures.text: The round red logo, free shipping and 24-minute in-store pickup. The company filed for Chapter 11 nine days later.[^14]
captures.warn: The main banner was a Flash file that the archive cannot play, so the capture shows an error message in its place.

captures.label: Under Systemax
captures.title: The same address, a different company
captures.text: Eight months after Systemax bought the name: a web-only store with the same logo and no shops.[^21]
